reforms.description: The Prosperity Initiative was launched as a consultation process aimed at identifying and building consensus around structural reforms to enhance the competitiveness of the Canadian economy.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The initiative aims to enhance competitiveness, which is expected to support economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiative has been launched and is in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant effort to reform and improve economic competitiveness.
reforms.source_quote: In 1992 the authorities launched the Prosperity Initiative, a consultation process to help identify, and build a consensus around, further structural reforms needed to improve the competitiveness of the economy.

reforms.description: The Canadian government increased support for R&D by providing additional funding to Canadian corporations undertaking research and development, while also streamlining access to R&D programmes and services.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased funding for R&D is expected to boost innovation and economic growth in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The government has successfully increased support and streamlined access.
reforms.importance_rationale: The increase in funding and improved access to R&D programmes represent significant enhancements to support for innovation.
reforms.source_quote: In its December 1992 Economic and Fiscal Statement, and again in the April 1993 Budget, the Government provided additional support to Canadian corporations undertaking R&D.
